digest.definition: Policing education serves a profession whose stated mission is safer communities through fair and firm law enforcement, crime prevention, keeping the peace, protection and bringing offenders to justice
distinctiveFeatures: Policing education serves a profession whose stated mission is safer communities through fair and firm law enforcement, crime prevention, keeping the peace, protection and bringing offenders to justice
It is professional education, shaped by a national drive to recognise policing as a profession, with the College of Policing setting standards in England and Wales

Its routes differ by nation: three licensed PEQF entry routes in England and Wales, no higher education entry route in Scotland, and a PSNI degree in Northern Ireland; unlicensed degrees still have value
Theory underpins applied practice: critical thinking, analysis and reflective learning through a curriculum that integrates theory and practice
Ethics and the Code of Ethics, the Peelian Principles and the Competency Values Framework are foundations of the learning
Evidence-based policing, problem-solving and research by practitioner-researchers are central
Employers and the professional body are closely involved, sometimes co-creating the degree with a police force
Teaching has moved from teacher-centred to learner-centred, experiential and co-produced learning

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: EDI is set at the core of the curriculum with ethics as a common thread; all students and stakeholders are to be treated fairly under the Public Sector Equality Duty, and students are to promote EDI and human rights in practice (D1, 1.16 to 1.19, 2.2, 3.2, 4.3)

widening access across physical and digital barriers, varied entry routes and flexible delivery, the 2018 accessibility regulations, and online provision suited to students with shift work, caring duties or a second language (D1, 1.19 to 1.23)

headed Sustainability, beside horizon scanning: programmes designed with the SDGs, with eight themes named for the Policing curriculum, including the environmental impact of policing and access to justice (D1, 1.24 to 1.26)

named as employability in the front matter: assessment co-designed with employers to enhance employability, the value of work-based learning, and job market skills among the SDG themes (D1, front matter, 1.26, 2.16, 3.14)

subjectSpecific.text: You will understand why policing has to meet the highest professional standards to be lawful, ethical, safe and effective.
You will be able to carry out your own research based on evidence.
You will come to understand how evidence-based policing and problem-solving work.
You will learn about several areas of front-line policing.
You will actively build equality, diversity, inclusion and human rights into how you work.
You will understand why looking after your wellbeing and resilience matters in policing.
You will understand how policing works in the digital world and how crime uses online tools.
You will build a thorough knowledge of policing, criminal justice and criminology.
You will understand how policing fits into the wider criminal justice system.
You will know the laws, powers and policies that govern policing and how they are used in practice.
You will recognise that a core duty of the police is to spot and support people who are vulnerable or at risk.
You will be able to choose and use specialist strategies to protect and support people who need it.
You will learn about national policing strategies, such as those on counter terrorism.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: students of the subject
statements.about: understanding of the profession and its legal setting
statements.paraphrase: The degree's main aim is to equip students with the knowledge, skills and behaviours of competent policing professionals; across the course students will build and show an understanding of the profession and of the legal and regulatory setting of policing and criminal justice.

forPractitioner.text: Plan the course so that, from start to finish, students will build and show an understanding of the policing profession and of the law and regulation that frame policing and the criminal justice system.

forBeneficiary.text: Across your course you will build and show an understanding of policing as a profession and of the laws and rules that shape policing and criminal justice.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: students of the subject
statements.paraphrase: In a safe space for trying out ideas and skills, students will develop effective communication and interpersonal skills, and many varied scenarios will ready them for what they meet as policing professionals.

forPractitioner.text: Give students a protected setting and a wide range of scenarios in which they will develop effective communication and interpersonal skills for professional policing.

forBeneficiary.text: In a safe setting with many practice scenarios, you will develop the communication and people skills that policing work needs.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: holders of a Policing degree
statements.about: judgement, evidence-informed decisions and linking theory to practice
statements.paraphrase: A Policing graduate will be able to weigh evidence, arguments and assumptions, judge soundly and convey those judgements well, and will have the qualities for work that calls for personal responsibility and decisions based on evidence in complex, unpredictable conditions; the graduate should also be able to build sound research, evidence-based techniques and problem-solving skills, and to connect theory with professional practice.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be able to evaluate evidence and argument, judge soundly, communicate well and decide responsibly on evidence in complex situations; they should also be able to use research, evidence-based practice and problem-solving at work and tie theory to practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to weigh up evidence and arguments, reach sound judgements, explain them clearly and make responsible decisions based on evidence in complex situations, linking what you learn to policing practice.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: a degree that excludes no group
statements.paraphrase: The characteristics of a Policing degree should show a system that neither discriminates against, ranks nor shuts out any group on grounds of protected characteristics, socioeconomic background or location.

forPractitioner.text: Check admissions, curriculum, teaching and assessment so the degree should show no discrimination, stratification or exclusion by protected characteristic, social background or where students live.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: fair treatment and equality impact assessment
statements.paraphrase: The subject's curriculum champions equality, diversity and inclusion; every student and stakeholder must be treated with openness, fairness, dignity and respect, and those designing courses should also consider an Equality Impact Assessment, done jointly with the force where a course is co-created.

forPractitioner.text: Treat every student and partner openly, fairly and with dignity: that is a must. Keep in view the Public Sector Equality Duty (Section 75 in Northern Ireland) and consider an Equality Impact Assessment, shared with the police force where you co-create the course.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: all students of Policing
statements.about: ethics as the highest standard of conduct
statements.paraphrase: EDI should be real concepts built into the culture and practice of the subject, with ethics running through the curriculum; all Policing students must understand why ethics matter as the highest standards and carry their learning into practice by owning their professional conduct.

forPractitioner.text: Embed EDI in the culture and practice of the course, operational or not, with ethics as a thread throughout; every student must understand ethics as the top standard and carry it into daily conduct, taking responsibility for their own behaviour.

forBeneficiary.text: You must understand why ethics sit at the heart of policing, put your learning into practice every day and take responsibility for behaving to the highest ethical standards.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: inclusive and accessible teaching and assessment
statements.paraphrase: The subject accepts that students learn in different ways and at different rates; inclusive teaching benefits everyone, and because variety alone may still exclude some, methods of teaching and assessment should be planned from the start to be inclusive and accessible.

forPractitioner.text: Design and plan teaching and assessment to be inclusive and accessible from the outset rather than adding variety later; varied styles on their own may still exclude some students.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Those offering Policing must show their commitment to widening access and to every student reaching their potential, attending to physical and digital barriers as well as to how students best take in and use knowledge.

forPractitioner.text: Show, with evidence, a commitment to widening access: address physical access, digital divides (devices and connectivity) and the wider design of teaching so every student can reach their potential.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Offering varied routes into police education widens participation; those offering the subject should stress flexible delivery so learning is accessible and the workforce recruited is more diverse and closer to the communities it serves.

forPractitioner.text: Stress flexible delivery and varied routes (work-based, knowledge-focused, graduate entry) so learning is accessible and recruits better reflect the communities they will serve.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: students, through the accessible provision of the course
statements.paraphrase: Students should be able to reach course support online so they can work round illness, travel problems or caring duties.

forPractitioner.text: Put support material online so students can keep studying through illness, transport trouble or family and caring commitments.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Policing degree

statements.paraphrase: Programmes should be designed with the UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals in mind; the statement names eight themes from them that a Policing curriculum can take up explicitly, from wellbeing and inclusive education to safe communities, environmental impact, just societies and partnership.

forPractitioner.text: Design the programme with reference to the SDGs, placing the eight named themes (wellbeing, inclusive education, equity, economic vitality and skills, safe communities, environmental impact, access to justice, partnership) openly in the curriculum.

statements.about: legislation, powers and policy in practice
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will know legislation, police powers and policy and how they apply in professional practice.

forPractitioner.text: Programmes will enable graduates to develop knowledge of legislation, powers and policy and of their use in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know the laws, powers and policies that govern policing and how they are used in practice.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject
statements.about: protecting people who are vulnerable or at risk
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will recognise that the police service has a basic duty to identify and professionally support people who are vulnerable or at risk.

forPractitioner.text: Programmes will enable graduates to recognise the service's core duty to identify and support vulnerable people and those at risk.

forBeneficiary.text: You will recognise that a core duty of the police is to spot and support people who are vulnerable or at risk.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will be able to choose and use suitable specialist strategies and techniques to support people who need public protection.

forPractitioner.text: Programmes will enable graduates to select and apply specialist strategies and techniques that protect people in need.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to choose and use specialist strategies to protect and support people who need it.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject
statements.about: national strategies such as counter terrorism
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will know national policing strategies, counter terrorism among them.

forPractitioner.text: Programmes will enable graduates to develop knowledge of national policing strategies, for instance on counter terrorism.

forBeneficiary.text: You will learn about national policing strategies, such as those on counter terrorism.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Programme design should be planned as a whole to build, assess and strengthen graduate skills that transfer to policing and beyond; every module should take account of reflection, critical thinking, decisions, communication, ethics, EDI, evidence-based practice, problem solving, leadership and teamwork.

forPractitioner.text: Plan the programme as a whole: each module should attend to reflective practice, critical thinking, decision-making, communication, ethics, EDI, evidence-based practice, problem-solving, styles of leadership and teamwork.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: the National Policing Curriculum in licensed programmes
statements.paraphrase: For a programme seeking the professional body's licence, the design must build the College of Policing's National Policing Curriculum into the degree and map learning so every element is covered; licensed programmes are also reviewed regularly and yearly by the body.

forPractitioner.text: If you seek College of Policing licensing, you must build the NPC into the degree and map learning so every element appears in the design; expect regular and annual professional review.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Staff associations matter for change across policing, and volunteers should also be formally represented when programmes are developed and reviewed, for example through students who volunteer as special constables.

forPractitioner.text: Formally involve volunteers, such as special constables and police support volunteers, in the consultations that develop and review the programme, alongside staff associations.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Current research in the discipline shapes how degrees are made and shows employers their worth; an evidence-based approach to creating degrees must follow other professions where experienced practitioner-researchers inform practice.

forPractitioner.text: When creating the degree, follow other professions in drawing on experienced practitioner-researchers; that evidence-based approach is a must and helps graduate skills transfer.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: joint honours students
statements.about: joint honours students and the core skills
statements.paraphrase: Joint honours students will reach the core subject-specific and generic skills of Policing and add others from their second subject, and may explore where the two overlap.

forPractitioner.text: Joint honours students will achieve the core subject and generic skills of Policing, adding others from the partner subject; leave room to explore the overlap.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study Policing with another subject, you will gain the core skills of Policing, add others from your second subject and can explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: final-year students on most policing, criminal justice and criminology programmes
statements.about: the independent final-year project or dissertation
statements.paraphrase: In the last year of most programmes in policing, criminal justice or criminology, students must design, carry out and finish an independent problem-based project or dissertation, normally showing maturity, handling the practical, ethical and organisational sides of research, engaging critically with evidence, literature, law and policy, and linking research to practice and policy.

forPractitioner.text: Require a final-year independent project or dissertation that each student must design, conduct and complete, in which they normally show mature research judgement, critical use of evidence, law and policy, and links to practice.

forBeneficiary.text: In your final year you must design, carry out and complete your own research project or dissertation, dealing with its practical and ethical sides and linking research to policing practice and policy.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: There should be a clear institutional strategy for partnership with other agencies that guides anyone entering such arrangements, which may cover whole courses or parts such as placements and may call for other sites, support or facilities.

forPractitioner.text: Set a clear institutional strategy for partnerships with agencies, covering whole courses or parts such as work placements, and plan for the sites, support and facilities they need.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: partners and the national qualifications framework
statements.paraphrase: Partners co-creating or delivering policing awards must satisfy the national qualifications framework that applies, and the awarding organisation should be responsible for making sure the standards are met.

forPractitioner.text: Partners must meet the relevant national qualifications framework (FHEQ or FQHEIS); the awarding organisation should carry the responsibility for assuring the standards.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: standards and student experience in partnerships
statements.paraphrase: The awarding body must make arrangements to keep the academic standard of the policing award; partnership input should also enrich the student experience, and where other agencies deliver some or all of the course there should be an effective process for managing and overseeing that experience.

forPractitioner.text: As awarding body you must have arrangements that hold the academic standard of the award; where agencies deliver part or all of the course, run an effective process to manage and oversee the whole student experience.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Policing degree

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: written partnership agreements and due diligence
statements.paraphrase: Partnerships for police qualifications should rest on legally binding written agreements setting out detailed arrangements and risks, with due diligence during the partnership and before renewal, governance recorded and kept current, and continuous monitoring by the awarding institution.

forPractitioner.text: Put each partnership on a legally binding written agreement that sets out arrangements and risks; carry out due diligence during it and before renewal; keep governance records current and monitor continuously.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Impartiality: the course should be designed so that students understand the context of the profession, uphold its standards and decide on objective grounds free of bias.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course so students learn to uphold professional standards and to decide on objective, impartial grounds, without bias or prejudice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student outcomes it serves are in 4.3

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Integrity: course content should reflect the highest standards expected of people in policing, including acting as a role model.

forPractitioner.text: Make content reflect the highest standards expected of people in policing, including being a role model.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student outcomes it serves are in 4.3

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Public service: course content should reflect that people in policing are responsible for acting in the best interests of society as a whole.

forPractitioner.text: Make content show that people in policing carry a responsibility to act in the best interests of society as a whole.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student outcomes it serves are in 4.3

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Transparency: policing awards should be designed so students understand why those working or volunteering in policing need to be open in their actions, decisions and communications.

forPractitioner.text: Design the award so students see why openness in actions, decisions and communication is needed of everyone working or volunteering in policing.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student outcomes it serves are in 4.3

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Diversity: policing awards should be designed so students understand and champion equality, diversity and inclusion in society.

forPractitioner.text: Design the award so students both understand equality, diversity and inclusion and champion them in society.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design; the student outcomes it serves are in 4.3

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: How a Policing degree is assessed depends partly on whether it is a licensed PEQF programme; licensed programmes require assessment that blends theory with the applied outcomes, ties to the workplace and the NPC and meets the academic provider's needs, and where it applies such assessment should map theory to practice as new constables also reach Independent Patrol Status and Full Occupational Competence.

forPractitioner.text: For licensed PEQF programmes (PCDA, DHEP) assessment is required to blend theory with application, reflect the student's own policing setting, link to the NPC and meet the academic awarding body's rules; it should map theory to practice alongside IPS and FOC.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: applied assessment blending theory and practice
statements.paraphrase: Academic and practical skills complement each other, so every Policing assessment, licensed or not, should centre on applied learning, let students show grounded theory and practice, test a mix of study and workforce-relevant skills, and give all students the chance to explore contemporary policing critically.

forPractitioner.text: Make every assessment applied: blend theory and practice, test academic and workforce-relevant skills together, and let all students explore contemporary policing critically, with debate and current research behind their learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: co-designed assessment and an assessment strategy
statements.paraphrase: Every provider of a Policing degree must be able to show that assessments were co-designed with police practitioners or other employers for a practice focus that helps employability, and every degree must have an assessment strategy that lets students show they have reached the right level and that supports learning.

forPractitioner.text: Co-design assessments with police practitioners or other employers and keep the evidence: that is a must. Have an assessment strategy that shows students reaching the required level and supports their learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should tie straight to the module's and the course's learning outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Align each assessment directly with the module and course learning outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should measure what students have learned: knowledge gained, understanding built and skills or abilities acquired.

forPractitioner.text: Make assessments measure the knowledge, understanding and skills students have actually gained.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: assessing the central aspects of outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Students should be assessed on the central parts of the learning outcomes, on what is taught and learned.

forPractitioner.text: Assess students on the core of the learning outcomes and on what the course actually teaches.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessment workload should be consistent and fair relative to credit value.

forPractitioner.text: Keep assessment workload consistent and fair across modules of the same credit value.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should support a path of progressive development for students across modules and levels.

forPractitioner.text: Sequence assessments so they build students' development from module to module and level to level.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should stress deep, active and reflective learning.

forPractitioner.text: Set assessments that reward deep, active and reflective learning rather than recall.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should actively and constructively improve how students learn.

forPractitioner.text: Use assessment to improve student learning, not only to grade it.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should centre on skills and on their transfer.

forPractitioner.text: Assess skills and whether students can carry them into new settings.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessments must put inclusivity at their core so all students' ways of learning are catered for and experience is equal.

forPractitioner.text: Build inclusion into the core of every assessment so all learning styles are met and students have a comparable experience: a must.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Assessment strategies must show that every student gets timely, detailed and relevant feedback.

forPractitioner.text: Show in the assessment strategy that every student receives timely, detailed and relevant feedback: a must.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.paraphrase: Those offering the degree should aim for a mix of assessments and new methods that draw students into active participation and critical reflection, with chances to show skills in writing, speech and visual form, alone and in groups and through independent research; they should show how student voice shapes the design of assessment and that inclusive assessment is considered.

forPractitioner.text: Use varied and innovative assessment (written, oral, visual; individual and group; independent research), show how student voice informs its design, and build in constructive alignment, clear criteria, timeliness, adaptability and constructive feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: full assessment information and a balance of methods
statements.paraphrase: Throughout the course students must receive full details of each assessment and the criteria or rubric used; there should be a fitting balance of diagnostic, formative and summative methods and chances in class or online to tackle challenging questions; applied assessment may take forms such as reflective writing, policy briefs, case studies, presentations or digital portfolios.

forPractitioner.text: Give students full details of every assessment and its criteria or rubric (a must); balance diagnostic, formative and summative assessment; give practice with challenging questions; consider applied forms such as policy briefs and digital portfolios.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: reviewing assessments for currency and integrity
statements.paraphrase: Assessments should be reviewed regularly to keep them current and valid and to reduce risks to academic integrity.

forPractitioner.text: Review assessments on a regular cycle so they stay current and valid and give little room for academic misconduct.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on those who design and run the course; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: those who design and run Policing degrees
statements.about: Annex D for achievement above the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will do much better than the minimum threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should refer to Annex D, which describes the four honours classes (1st, 2:1, 2:2 and 3rd) for honours at FHEQ level 6 and FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Decide what evidence shows achievement above the threshold, and use the Annex D descriptions of the four honours classes when you judge it.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: tells the course how to judge achievement above the threshold; the student-facing standards are 4.3 and 4.4

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, applies a deep understanding of how policing, criminal justice and criminology connect to present or future professional duties.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply an in-depth grasp of how policing, criminal justice and criminology interlock to their professional responsibilities, now or later.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can apply a deep understanding of how policing, criminal justice and criminology fit together to your current or future work.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands and judges how criminal law is applied in policing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand and evaluate the way criminal law is applied to policing.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand how criminal law is applied in policing and can judge how well it is applied.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, applies thorough knowledge and understanding of policing that is safe, lawful and effective.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates bring a deep knowledge of what makes policing safe, lawful and effective to bear on practice.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use detailed knowledge of what makes policing safe, lawful and effective.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands several specialisms within policing, for example response, community and roads policing, intelligence and investigation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand several policing specialisms, for example response, neighbourhood, roads, intelligence and investigation.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand several policing specialisms, such as response, community and roads policing, intelligence and investigation.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, chooses and uses suitable current policing strategies in complex, interrelated contexts.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates select and apply fitting contemporary policing strategies to complex, interconnected situations.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can choose and use suitable modern policing strategies in complex situations where many factors interact.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, applies broad knowledge and understanding of digital policing and crime involving technology.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply broad knowledge of digital policing and of crime that involves technology.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use a broad knowledge of digital policing and of crime that involves technology.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: an ethical approach and professional values
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands and takes an ethical approach in line with the police service's highest professional values and standards.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand and adopt an ethical stance matching the service's highest professional values and standards.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand and take an ethical approach that matches the highest professional values of the police service.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: promoting equality, diversity, inclusion and human rights
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, takes personal responsibility for advancing equality, diversity, inclusivity and human rights.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates take personal responsibility for promoting equality, diversity, inclusion and human rights.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you take personal responsibility for promoting equality, diversity, inclusion and human rights.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: supporting victims, witnesses and the vulnerable
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, brings together specialist current theories, ideas and methods that can be used to support victims, witnesses, vulnerable people and those at risk.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates synthesise specialist, interconnected theories and methods for supporting victims, witnesses and people who are vulnerable or at risk.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can combine specialist theories and methods to support victims, witnesses and people who are vulnerable or at risk.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: preventing and detecting crime; suspects and offenders
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, uses specialist current theories and methods to prevent crime, detect it, and deal with suspects and offenders.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates adopt specialist, interconnected theories and methods to prevent and detect crime and to handle suspects and offenders.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use specialist theories and methods to prevent and detect crime and to deal with suspects and offenders.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, critically judges evidence-based research and applies it to the complexities of policing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates critically evaluate evidence-based research and apply it to complex policing problems.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can critically judge research evidence and use it on complex policing problems.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, chooses and uses specialist strategies, methods and research evidence to solve complex problems.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates select and apply specialist strategies, methods and research evidence to complex problem solving.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can choose and use specialist methods and research evidence to work through complex problems.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, makes informed decisions in complex, unpredictable and interrelated situations, based on critical thinking and evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates make informed decisions in complex, unpredictable, interconnected situations, grounded in critical thinking and evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can make informed decisions in complex and unpredictable situations, based on critical thinking and evidence.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, works within chosen guidelines and uses professional discretion.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates act within selected guidelines and exercise professional discretion.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can work within the relevant guidelines and use professional discretion well.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands and uses conflict management skills.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand and apply the skills of managing conflict.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand and can use the skills of managing conflict.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, applies a deep understanding of leadership, teamwork and working in partnership.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply an in-depth understanding of leadership, team working and partnership working.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use a deep understanding of leadership, teamwork and working with partner agencies.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: wellbeing and resilience of self and others
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands and uses techniques that protect their own and others' wellbeing and resilience in every situation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand and apply techniques that keep themselves and others well and resilient in all situations.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand and use techniques to look after your own and others' wellbeing and resilience in any situation.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, reflects on self actively and continually, developing ways to improve own practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates engage actively in continual self-reflection and develop strategies to improve their practice.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you reflect on your own work actively and continually and find ways to improve it.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: research design, collection, analysis and interpretation
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, uses a range of established techniques accurately to design research and to collect, analyse and interpret data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates accurately deploy established techniques to design research and to gather, analyse and interpret its data.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use established research techniques accurately to design a study and to gather, analyse and interpret data.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: communicating to specialist and lay audiences
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, organises and conveys connected information for specialist and non-specialist audiences.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates organise and communicate interconnected information to specialist and lay audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can organise connected information and explain it to experts and to people outside policing.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, critically judges arguments, assumptions and abstract ideas to find possible solutions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates critically evaluate arguments, assumptions and abstract concepts to find possible solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can critically judge arguments, assumptions and abstract ideas to find possible solutions.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: autonomy and responsibility in complex contexts
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, works independently and takes responsibility for personal or group tasks in complex settings.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates act autonomously and take responsibility for individual or group tasks in complex settings.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can work on your own initiative and take responsibility for your own and group tasks in complex settings.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.about: political, economic, social, technological, environmental, legal and ethical debates
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, appreciates today's debates affecting the discipline, whether political, economic, social, technological, environmental, legal or ethical.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates appreciate the live political, economic, social, technological, environmental, legal and ethical debates that shape policing as a discipline.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand today's debates that affect policing, whether political, economic, social, technological, environmental, legal or ethical.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands current debates on equality, diversity, inclusion and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand contemporary debates on equality, diversity, inclusion and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand current debates about equality, diversity, inclusion and sustainability.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, understands how culture affects ways of working.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand the effect of culture on working practices.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you understand how culture shapes the way people work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, uses at work a range of innovative methods and techniques learned on the course.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply a range of innovative methods and techniques they have learned to employment.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can use a range of new methods and techniques you have learned in your work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, chooses and uses a range of digital skills and techniques at work.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates choose and use a range of digital skills and techniques at work.

forBeneficiary.text: At the threshold, you can choose and use a range of digital skills and tools at work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the threshold level
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, reflects actively on self to find and meet own learning needs.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates engage actively in self-reflection to identify and address their own learning needs.
